_anchors.canvas.w: 56, and it is square with the height because THE BODY TURNS OVER. A somersault sweeps the sprite through every angle, so the cell has to hold the body's own diagonal — 34 px tall by 30 wide is a 45 px diagonal, and 56 holds it with the outline ring and margin at the worst angle. A cell sized for the rest pose would clip the skull at 45 degrees.
_anchors.canvas.h: 56, square with the width, for the same reason.
_anchors.canvas.originX: 28, dead centre, and it is the FIRST subject in this project that must be centred. Every other body was anchored where it stands; this one rotates about its hips, so the origin has to be the centre of rotation or the whole sprite orbits its own cell.
_anchors.canvas.originY: 30. The hip joint, and the rotation centre. The scene anchors him by his lowest painted pixel, which moves through the flip and is meaningless during it — the runtime holds him by his own hip row while he is in the air.
_anchors.tones.perMaterial: 5, the Chrono idiom, and the SOTN reference spends it asymmetrically: four of the bone's five tones sit below the midpoint.
_anchors.frames.walk: 6, and the clip PLAYS ONCE. `Gait.wrap` is false, so the six frames span the motion end to end rather than looping — the last frame is the apex pose and the runtime holds it until he lands.
_anchors.light.x: -0.5, upper left, as every subject except the astronaut.
_anchors.light.y: -0.62, and it is LOWER than the garden's -0.72. A graveyard at night is lit from a moon near the horizon, and a low lamp is what puts a rim on a skull instead of a wash over it.
_anchors.light.z: -0.22, barely toward the viewer. Less front light than the kitten: SOTN wants the form to fall away, so the light grazes.
_anchors.light.curve: 1.3, and it is the highest in the project. Above 1 the dark end compresses into a rim, which is exactly the SOTN value structure — a mass that reads as one dark shape with a bright edge on it.
_anchors.gait.swing: 0.42 turns, 151 degrees. The widest cyclic amplitude here, and it is derived from the stride: a sprinting figure's thigh swings about 130 degrees between contact and reach, and the keys are fractions of that.
_anchors.gait.lift: 4 px. The hips bounce 2 px either way over a stride. A skeleton has no muscle to absorb a landing, so it runs high and rigid — a third of the gorilla's drop on a body of similar height.
_anchors.gait.depth: 6 px. Unused; every clip is authored in the screen plane, which is the finding of this round.
_anchors.gait.roll: 0 = no roll. Turns, and it is a SEPARATE amplitude from gait.swing on purpose: swing is a walk range (0.08 of a turn) and a flip is a whole one. Run 7 spent a walk amplitude on a jump and lost a limb in every frame; one knob across a 12x range would guarantee it a third time.
_anchors.body.scale: 1. He stands 34 px in a 240 px world, a seventh of the width — the runner proportion, where a player needs to read three obstacles ahead.
_anchors.texture.dither: 0 = the hard cut this sample shipped with, and it is the null case: at 0 the dither term is exactly 0 and the render is byte-for-byte what it was. Turned on per subject, never globally, because the weave is an idiom decision and not a fix.
_anchors.texture.lattice: 4. Size of the ordered dither lattice, 2 or 4. MEASURED rather than chosen: a 4x4 weave needs a 4x4 patch of one surface to be visible, and this project s characters have none — the rider at 36 px scores 0.000 on that share, the skeleton 0.080, the kitten 0.068, a kerb 0.432. Switching both outlines off moved it not at all; doubling the body scale moved it to 0.177, so the cause is scale and not the line. 2 is what fits a small body; 4 is for a road or a sky. Read it with the [weave] line of `node bin/bench.ts`.
_anchors.shadow.steps: 7, one more than the deepest mass (the ribcage at 4.2, the shroud at 3).
_anchors.shadow.strength: 2 ramp steps, against the garden's 1. A graveyard at night has one moon and nothing to bounce it — the same reasoning that put the moon scene at 2.
_anchors.fill.weight: 0.06, against the garden's 0.16. Almost no bounce: there is no foliage overhead and the ground is wet stone. The declared cost of a fill is that it compresses the value range, and this is the one subject in the project that cannot afford to lose any.
_anchors.playback.msPerFrame: 60. Six frames make a 360 ms launch, which is about the time the body spends going up before gravity owns it.
_anchors.outline.material: "ink". Near black with a blue cast, because the ground is indigo and a warm line would separate from the scene rather than from the body.
_anchors.outline.inner: true, and `Part.weld` decides where it actually lands. Every solid on this body is welded EXCEPT the jaw: a jaw line is a real seam, and it is the edge that makes a skull read as a skull instead of an egg.
